articles.description:
Remote teams live on shared files. Contracts, screenshots, slide exports, scanned receipts and product photos move between people all day. When file habits are sloppy, small problems pile up: emails bounce because attachments are too big, people review the wrong version, and confidential documents end up on random websites. After a few years of remote work, our team settled on a handful of habits that remove most of this friction.
1. Agree on formats
Decide as a team which formats you use for what. Our simple rules: PDF for anything that should look fixed, such as contracts, reports and invoices; PNG for screenshots with text; JPG or WebP for photos; and the original source file kept in shared storage for anything still being edited. Clear defaults prevent endless "I can't open this" messa…

articles.author: Sujal Khatri
articles.description:
A URL slug is the readable tail of a link — the part after the domain. For example, in example.com/blog/10-ways-to-fix-your-garden-spring-2026, the slug is "10-ways-to-fix-your-garden-spring-2026". A clean slug helps readers and search engines understand the page before they click it.
The rules are simple:
All lowercase — mixed case in URLs causes duplicate-content confusion.
Words joined with hyphens, not underscores or spaces.
No special characters — question marks, exclamation marks, ampersands and em dashes have to go.
Accents transliterated — "Café Menu 2026" becomes "cafe-menu-2026", not a broken string of percent-codes.
Short beats long — keeping a slug under about 60 characters is a good rule of thumb. Cut filler words rather than the meaning.
Examples:
Doing this by hand for one post is fine. Doing it for fifty posts is where a tool earns its keep. I built a free one that does exactly this in your browser — paste a title, the slug appears as you type, nothing uploads anywhere: https://bulktextkit.gt.tc/tools/slug-generator.php?utm_source=devto
One last line, not a pitch: the same site's Pro plan ($19 one-time) adds a bulk mode that turns 50 titles into 50 slugs at once; the free slug tool itself stays free.
articles.title: How to Turn Any Blog Title Into a Clean URL Slug (and Why It Matters for SEO)
